dedupe_keys.name: iceland optimal helicopter ambulance base locations to minimise pre hospital times

description: This case study applies facility location optimisation to decide where Iceland should place additional helicopter ambulance bases. The authors published it as an open-access journal article. Because few hospitals in Iceland can treat time-sensitive conditions and the population is spread thinly, the models consider three transport modes, ground ambulances, fixed-wing air ambulances and helicopters, and add new helicopter bases to the existing fixed-wing base, helicopter base and ground ambulance stations. The primary objective maximises the share of incidents covered and the secondary objective minimises patient transport cost, using incident locations and travel times for each mode. Coverage is the whole of Iceland. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives licence. Caveats: results depend on the assumption about which hospital receives patients, weather limits on flying are simplified, and costs of operating new bases are outside the model. The study found that Akureyri and Flúðir are the best candidates for a second helicopter base, with Flúðir better if all patients go to Reykjavík and Akureyri better if patients go to the nearest hospital. Simulation uses: an example of optimisation for emergency medical service investment appraisal in sparsely populated regions. Related records: the Norway Air-Mobile Stroke Unit siting study (case_study-norway-air-mobile-stroke-unit-base-optimisation) uses a similar coverage model.
